content.title: How to Start Selling Digital Products with Crypto Payments

content.text: What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Crypto payment

A sovereign digital commerce stack is a complete combination of free and paid tools that gives creators a fully operational online store with automatic crypto payment processing, instant product delivery, and full data ownership. This matters because it allows creators to maintain control over their sales, customer data, and revenue, without being beholden to platform fees or restrictions. For example, Gumroad charges 10% on every sale, while NOWPayments charges only 0.5%, resulting in significant savings for creators.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

The architecture of a sovereign digital commerce stack typically consists of a hosting platform like GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, a backend logic platform like Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, and a payment processing platform like NOWPayments. These components work together to enable automatic crypto payment verification, instant product delivery, and secure data storage. For instance, when a customer makes a payment, the NOWPayments platform verifies the transaction and triggers a webhook that delivers the product to the customer's email or download link.
Who This Is Built For and Why

This solution is built for digital creators in regions where conventional payment platforms are unavailable or restricted. These creators sell a wide range of digital products, including ebooks, courses, templates, fonts, and software. By using a sovereign digital commerce stack, they can reach a global audience, receive payments in cryptocurrency, and maintain control over their sales and customer data. This is particularly important for creators who want to build a sustainable and independent business, without relying on platforms that may change their terms or fees at any time.
Sovereign digital commerce stacks enable creators to maintain control over their sales, customer data, and revenue.
The Components That Make It Work Together

The components of a sovereign digital commerce stack include hosting, backend logic, payment processing, and storage. Each component plays a critical role in enabling the stack to function seamlessly. For example, Cloudflare Workers provides a serverless platform for backend logic, while Supabase provides a secure and scalable storage solution for customer data and product information. By integrating these components, creators can build a robust and reliable commerce stack that meets their needs and grows with their business.
How to Use This Knowledge to Deploy Today

To deploy a sovereign digital commerce stack today, creators can start by selecting the components that best fit their needs. They can choose from a range of hosting platforms, backend logic platforms, and payment processing platforms, and integrate these components using APIs and webhooks. The Complete Builder Kit ($197) provides a comprehensive solution, including all 6 blueprints and 7 templates, to help creators build, deploy, and scale their commerce stack. With this knowledge, creators can take control of their sales, customer data, and revenue, and build a sustainable and independent business online.

To sell an ebook online without PayPal or Stripe, creators can use a sovereign digital commerce stack that integrates a payment processing platform like NOWPayments. This platform enables automatic crypto payment verification, instant product delivery, and secure data storage, without relying on conventional payment platforms. By using a sovereign commerce stack, creators can maintain control over their sales, customer data, and revenue, and reach a global audience without platform restrictions or fees.

Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy a sovereign digital commerce stack, creators can follow these steps: select a hosting platform like GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, choose a backend logic platform like Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, integrate a payment processing platform like NOWPayments, set up storage for customer data and product information, and configure APIs and webhooks to enable seamless integration. By following these steps, creators can build a robust and reliable commerce stack that meets their needs and grows with their business.
